title: The Fibonacci Quilt game: a linear bound on game length
statement: Every game of the Fibonacci Quilt game of Miller and Newlon on n lasts at most (23/10) n + 2.95 moves (exact rational potential: explicit weights for indices < 31 and u_i = 2.3 q_i - i/3 - beta beyond; every rule except the once-only rule 2(a) lowers the potential by at least 1). The longest games, computed exhaustively for n <= 90, first equal 2n at n = 78, first exceed it at n = 86, and reach 2.022n at n = 89; numerically, potentials of this shape do not go below about 2.29.
resolves: Miller and Newlon (2020) open question 'Is there a reasonable upper bound on the length of a game?', by a linear bound with an exact certificate
verified: fq_bound.py: every rule instance with indices <= 200 lowers the potential by >= 1 in exact rational arithmetic; the closed-form tail reduces to four inequalities that hold; u_i <= 2.3 q_i; exhaustive longest games for n <= 40 within the bound; lowering alpha to 2.2 breaks the certificate.
fq_longest_exhaustive.cpp: exhaustive longest games for n <= 90 (about 11 million states), all within the bound; first length >= 2n at n = 78; maximum ratio 2.022 at n = 89.

Independent review (fresh agent): rules re-typed from the paper, certificate re-derived exactly for indices <= 400, exhaustive longest games re-run with independent code (11,408,896 states, all values matching), Lemma 2.2 (rule 2(a) at most once) checked exhaustively on all 78,464 positions where 2(a) is the only move (other indices <= 40) under three readings of rule 3(f).

fq_strategy.cpp: a fixed priority strategy (evidence/fq_long_strategy.json) plays legal games of length 2231, 22718, 227740, 2278223 on n = 10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6 (2.2782n at 10^6), so the longest game there is within [2.2782n, 2.3n + 2.95].
unresolved: the exact asymptotic constant of the longest game (between about 2.278, from an explicit strategy, and 2.3 proved; the potential-method limit is about 2.2899)
a general proof of Lemma 2.2 for the value-preserving reading of rule 3(f) beyond the computational check
nonclaims: 2.3 is not claimed optimal; the potential-method limit of about 2.29 is a numerical LP observation
rule 3(f) is read as q5,q7 because the printed q3,q7 does not preserve value
smallest_decisive_test: A rule instance lowering the potential by less than 1, or a game on n longer than 2.3 n + 2.95.
